_note: Research output of an unverified site-selection agent (FSRE session, 2026-09-12). Numbers are descriptive, in-sample, and not yet reproduced by committed code or tests.

chosen.reservoir: Ridgway Reservoir on the Uncompahgre River near Ridgway, Colorado (USGS-09147022; Reclamation's Dallas Creek Project; the maximum storage in the window is 83,400 acre-ft). Canyon Lake, TX was checked and ranks lower (see alternatives).
chosen.storage_series: USGS-09147022 'RIDGWAY RESERVOIR NEAR RIDGWAY, CO', parameter 00054 (Reservoir storage), statistic_id 00003 (computation_identifier 'Mean', i.e. the DAILY MEAN, not end-of-day), unit 'Acre-ft', time_series_id 797314f325e34cf786b0fdf2f8ad5094, primary. The metadata record runs 1990-09-30 to 2026-09-10. It is the only daily storage statistic at this site: there is no 32400 (value at 24:00) series and no daily elevation series. Because the storage is a daily mean, S(d+1)-S(d) spans noon(d) to noon(d+1). A centered alignment, 0.5*(net(d)+net(d+1)), gives a residual SD of 20.6 cfs, against 27.4 cfs for same-day alignment and 32.3 cfs for previous-day alignment. Over 2022-10-01..2025-09-30 the values span 51,520-83,400 acre-ft (mean 67,332).
outflow_series: USGS-09147025 UNCOMPAHGRE RIVER BELOW RIDGWAY RESERVOIR, CO; 00060 daily mean (00003), ft^3/s, time_series_id 90cdb4f56c3949ea8aefebc25403a97c, record 1988-10-01..2026-09-10, DA 265 sq mi (equal to the lake DA). It sits just below the dam at 38.2406N, versus 38.2372N for the lake gauge. No separate spillway or bypass gauge exists (the bbox search found only discontinued sites 09146550, 09146600 and 09172100). Spill and hydropower releases pass this gauge. Window mean 171.3 cfs (range 33.2-912).
inflow_series: USGS-09146200 UNCOMPAHGRE RIVER NEAR RIDGWAY, CO; 00060 daily mean, time_series_id 91f23a98ea974568bd417404233a31ca, record 1958-10-01..2026-09-10, DA 149 sq mi; window mean 141.0 cfs (31.4-1020); 82 of 1096 values ESTIMATED

USGS-09147000 DALLAS CREEK NEAR RIDGWAY, CO; 00060 daily mean, time_series_id 2a8d8d7edd56488ebd48fed56e6676dd, record 1922-03-01..2026-09-10, DA 97.2 sq mi; window mean 28.5 cfs (0.07-273); 290 of 1096 values ESTIMATED (mostly winter/ice, presumably)
chosen.drainage_areas: All values come from the monitoring-locations 'drainage_area' field. Lake site USGS-09147022: 265 sq mi. Outflow USGS-09147025: 265 sq mi. Inflow USGS-09146200: 149 sq mi. Inflow USGS-09147000: 97.2 sq mi. Gauged inflow area is 246.2 sq mi, leaving 18.8 sq mi (7.1%) ungauged: Beaver Creek through the town of Ridgway plus the lake-local area. Cow Creek joins below the dam and is not part of the 265.
chosen.common_window: 2022-10-01 to 2025-09-30 (water years 2023-2025, 1096 days). All four series have a value on every day, with no nulls, and all 4 x 1096 values are 'Approved'. A provisional probe over the window returned 0 rows. The latest last_modified is 2026-03-11, and time-series-revisions returned 0 records for the four sites. ESTIMATED qualifier counts: storage 2, Uncompahgre nr Ridgway 82, Dallas Ck 290, outflow 1. Data after 2025-09-30 exist (metadata end 2026-09-10) but were not retrieved and are presumably provisional. Descriptive in-sample closure check (no fitted parameters, no held-out evaluation, nothing beyond these 3 years is shown): with centered alignment, residual mean 0.73 cfs and SD 20.6 cfs; predicted versus observed dS has correlation 0.993 and NSE 0.982. By water year the residual (mean/SD) is WY2023 1.65/21.8, WY2024 2.51/20.9 and WY2025 -1.98/18.7 cfs. The 3-year cumulative imbalance is -750 cfs-days, -0.4% of 185,824 cfs-days of inflow. Monthly mean residuals run from -46 cfs (2025-06) to +47 cfs (2023-08): negative in May-June (snowmelt, evaporation or inflow-gauge bias) and positive in the Aug-2023 monsoon (ungauged local inflow). Evaporation, ungauged inflow and gauge error are not separated here.
chosen.daily_time_semantics: The daily 'time' property is a bare calendar date with no zone (e.g. "2025-09-10"). The API's only definition is "The date an observation represents". The daily schema and the 1.8 MB OpenAPI document never say which time zone defines the day: no match for 'midnight', 'standard time' or 'local' in that sense. The server treats it as a floating date. Probes on 2025-06-15 with time windows at 03:00-04:00Z, 07:00-08:00Z and 23:00-23:30Z all returned that date's single value, so query hours are not converted. The four Ridgway sites report time_zone_abbreviation 'MST' and uses_daylight_savings 'Y'. The time-series-metadata begin/end fields show day starts as local civil midnight WITH daylight saving, e.g. 2026-09-10T06:00:00+00:00 (MDT) versus 1958-10-01T07:00:00 (MST). Arizona sites flagged uses_daylight_savings 'N' also show 06:00Z in summer, so these offsets are not authoritative. Legacy NWIS practice is to compute daily values over the site's local STANDARD-time day, which for Ridgway would be 07:00Z to 07:00Z. This API does not state that and I did not verify it, so DAF should either declare it as an assumption with citation or refuse to assign UTC day bounds.
chosen.complications: (1) Storage is a daily MEAN (00003), so it is half a day out of step with daily-mean flows; use centered/trapezoidal alignment (SD 20.6 cfs centered vs 27.4 same-day). (2) The 7.1% ungauged area, including Beaver Creek, shows up as positive residuals in monsoon months (+47 cfs mean in 2023-08). (3) Winter ice: 290 Dallas Ck and 82 Uncompahgre values are ESTIMATED. (4) Evaporation is not measured. For a roughly 1,000-acre surface at about 6,900 ft it should be a few cfs, small next to the 171 cfs mean outflow; this surface-area figure comes from memory, not from the API, so it needs a citation or should be treated as a fitted parameter. Daily precipitation series (00045, statistic 00006) exist at 09147000 and 09147025 as optional lake-surface covariates. (5) Diversions: no USGS-gauged withdrawals or bypasses at the reservoir. I found no direct municipal intake (from memory, unverified). Irrigation ditches between the inflow gauges and the reservoir head are possible but unverified. Ridgway hydropower discharges through the outlet above gauge 09147025. (6) Travel times: both inflow gauges are about 2-5 km above the reservoir head (38.18N, lake body 38.20-38.24N) and the outflow gauge is at the dam, so all are well under 1 day. (7) Snowmelt peaks up to 1,020 cfs (May-June) are where the largest negative monthly residuals occur (-46 cfs in 2025-06). (8) Storage comes from a stage-capacity table (not published in the API), so capacity-table revisions would move S.
chosen.rationale: Every criterion is met: (1) a primary daily 00054 acre-ft series; (2) an outflow gauge immediately below the dam, with no separate spillway or bypass; (3) inflow gauges on both major tributaries, 0.929 gauged by area; (4) three recent, fully approved water years with no gaps; (5) no known large unmeasured withdrawals and small evaporation relative to the flows; (6) sub-day travel times. The descriptive closure over those three years supports the choice: residual SD 20.6 cfs against about 170 cfs of throughput, NSE 0.982, 3-year imbalance -0.4% of inflow. Higher-fraction alternatives lose on unmeasured fluxes: San Carlos (0.970), Milford (0.986) and Kanopolis (0.965) face evaporation comparable to low inflows. Horseshoe+Bartlett (0.951) has desert evaporation and monsoon inflow from about 300 ungauged sq mi. Lake Mohave (0.991) has no recent outflow data. Canyon Lake (0.918) has no storage series since 2002 and unmeasured GBRA withdrawals. The main weakness at Ridgway is that storage is a daily mean rather than end-of-day, which needs centered alignment.

alternatives: 2. Horseshoe + Bartlett reservoirs (Verde River, AZ), treated as one system. Storage: USGS-09509501 and USGS-09509502, both 00054 statistic 32400 (end-of-day midnight reading; 1974-). Inflow: USGS-09508500 Verde blw Tangle Ck (DA 5858). Outflow: USGS-09510000 Verde blw Bartlett Dam (DA 6161). Gauged fraction 5858/6161 = 0.951. Pros: end-of-day storage aligns exactly with daily-mean flows; no known direct withdrawals (SRP diverts downstream at Granite Reef); short travel times. Cons: unmeasured Sonoran-desert evaporation on two lakes (rough memory estimate tens of cfs versus summer baseflow of about 150 cfs); about 300 sq mi of ungauged desert with monsoon flash inflows; two storage gauges to sum. Daily values not retrieved (budget), so approval is unverified.

3. San Carlos Reservoir (Gila River, AZ). Storage: USGS-09469000, 00054 statistic 32400 (1982-) and 00003 (1987-), plus 00065 32400 'Lake Elevation at Midnight'. Inflows: USGS-09466500 Gila at Calva (DA 11470) and USGS-09468500 San Carlos R nr Peridot (DA 1026). Outflow: USGS-09469500 Gila blw Coolidge Dam (DA 12886). Gauged fraction 12496/12886 = 0.970. Pros: end-of-day storage; no direct withdrawals (irrigation diversion is downstream). Cons: a large, variable lake surface with desert evaporation that can match dry-season inflows (estimated, not measured); seasonal releases; long reach from Calva, which may approach 1 day. Daily values not retrieved.

4. Kanopolis Lake (Smoky Hill River, KS). Storage: USGS-06865000, 00054 statistic 00003 (daily mean, 2003-), plus 62614 elevation. Inflow: USGS-06864500 Smoky Hill R at Ellsworth (DA 7580). Outflow: USGS-06865500 Smoky Hill R nr Langley (DA 7857). Gauged fraction 7580/7857 = 0.965. Cons: daily-mean storage; unmeasured evaporation against very low 2022-23 drought inflows; winter ice; about 20 river miles from Ellsworth.

5. Milford Lake (Republican River, KS). Storage: USGS-06857050, 00054 statistic 00003 (2002-). Inflow: USGS-06856600 Republican R at Clay Center (DA 24542, contributing 17042). Outflow: USGS-06857100 Republican R at Junction City (DA 24900). Gauged fraction 24542/24880 = 0.986, the highest by area. Cons: daily-mean storage; a large lake (about 16,000 acres, from memory) with evaporation comparable to low flows; ice; large non-contributing area.

6. Canyon Lake (Guadalupe River, TX), the suggested candidate. Its 00054 storage series (statistic 32400) ENDED 2002-09-30. Only elevation remains: 62614 NGVD29 daily mean since 1992 plus max/min since 1988, so storage would need an external TWDB elevation-capacity table. Inflow: USGS-08167500 Guadalupe Rv nr Spring Branch (DA 1315). Outflow: USGS-08167800 Guadalupe Rv at Sattler (DA 1436). Lake DA 1432, so gauged fraction 1315/1432 = 0.918. Cons: GBRA and other direct withdrawals from the lake are not USGS-gauged (magnitude unknown here; roughly 10-20 cfs from memory); evaporation; very low 2022-24 drought inflows. Fails criterion (1) as preferred.

7. Boca Reservoir (Little Truckee River, CA). Storage: USGS-10344490, 00054 statistic 32400 (2006-), plus 62614 elevation. Inflow: USGS-10344400 Little Truckee ab Boca (DA 146). Outflow: USGS-10344500 Little Truckee bl Boca Dam (DA 173). Gauged fraction 146/172 = 0.849. End-of-day storage and short travel times, but 15% of the area is ungauged high-elevation snowmelt.

8. Choke Canyon Reservoir (Frio River, TX). Storage: USGS-08206900, 00054 statistics 00003 and 30600 (0600 reading). Inflows: USGS-08206600 Frio at Tilden (DA 4493) and USGS-08206700 San Miguel Ck nr Tilden (DA 783). Outflow: USGS-08206910 OWC (DA 5490). Gauged fraction 5276/5490 = 0.961. Evaporation-dominated, with near-zero inflow in drought.

9. Lake Mohave (Colorado River, AZ-NV). Storage: USGS-09422500, 00054 statistic 32400. Inflow: USGS-09421500 below Hoover Dam (DA 171700). Outflow: USGS-09423000 below Davis Dam (DA 173300). Gauged fraction 0.991, but the outflow's daily 00060 series ENDS 2022-10-02, so there is no recent common window. Storage change is also a small difference of about 10,000 cfs flows.

Dropped at screening: Perry Lake KS (the only active inflow is USGS-06890100, DA 431 of 1141 = 0.38). Lake Corpus Christi (fraction 0.944, but it sits downstream of Choke Canyon releases and has municipal withdrawals). Most Oklahoma, north-Texas and Front-Range water-supply lakes (Tawakoni, Lake Fork, Cedar Creek, Richland-Chambers, Atoka, Eucha/Spavinaw, Lake Worth, Houston, Conroe): large pipeline withdrawals not gauged by USGS. Lahontan, Milner, Havasu, Tulloch and Don Pedro: large canal or aqueduct diversions.
api_notes:
Base URL: https://api.waterdata.usgs.gov/ogcapi/v1. /ogcapi/v0/collections still answers, but its links point to v1. Collections used: time-series-metadata, monitoring-locations, daily, time-series-revisions, plus the landing page and openapi. The legacy waterservices.usgs.gov was not needed and not contacted.

Filtering:
- Comma-separated lists work for monitoring-locations 'id' and for time-series-metadata / time-series-revisions 'monitoring_location_id'; 105 ids in one URL (about 1.5 KB) was fine.
- 'bbox' works on time-series-metadata, so one request per candidate found nearby discharge series.
- Useful filters: parameter_code, computation_period_identifier=Daily, statistic_id, time_series_id, approval_status, time.
- Daily storage (00054) statistics seen: 32400 (value at 24:00, 381 series), 00003 (mean, 138), 30800/30600 (08:00/06:00 readings), and max/min. 831 daily 00054 series in total; 105 sites are active with begin <= 2023.

Pagination:
- OGC 'limit' defaults to 100, max 10000 per the OpenAPI.
- Paging is cursor-based: a rel='next' link carries ?cursor=...; the last page has no next link. numberMatched is not returned.
- Items come back in no time order, so sort client-side. The docs say 'sortby' limits the result to a single page.
- Example: 1096 days with limit=500 took 3 pages; limit=2000 returned everything in one page.

Daily item fields: time_series_id, monitoring_location_id, parameter_code, statistic_id, time (YYYY-MM-DD), value (a STRING, to preserve precision), unit_of_measure, approval_status (Approved/Provisional), qualifier (list or null, e.g. ['ESTIMATED']), last_modified. The per-feature id is a random UUID.

Non-primary series are retained for only 120 days, per the schema.

Rate limits and caching:
- 33 keyless requests over about 11 minutes: no HTTP 429 or 5xx, and no X-RateLimit headers returned.
- The OpenAPI documents 429 OVER_RATE_LIMIT, suggesting an API key; no key was used and no account was created.
- Responses go through CloudFront with 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600'. The first collections response had Age 34687 s, so a response can be cached content. Record Age/X-Cache alongside the sha256.
- The client sent User-Agent 'FSRE-DAF-research-client/0.1 (reservoir water-balance site selection...)' with exponential backoff on 429/5xx (never triggered).

Budget used: 23 metadata requests (one was a first attempt lost to a local log-path bug and repeated), well under 150. 10 daily-values requests covered 4 series, each limited to 2022-10-01..2025-09-30 (3 years). That count includes a provisional probe and 3 one-day time-semantics probes on the storage series.

Provenance log (URL, retrieved_at, status, sha256, bytes) is at C:\Users\jason\AppData\Local\Temp\usgs_sel\requests.jsonl. Raw daily JSON is in dv_*.json in the same directory. No repository writes.
